summary:
COSCOM proposes ROVER (Robotic Operations for Valuable Equipment Recovery), a conceptual robotic recovery system designed to identify and collect abandoned human-made equipment on the Moon and Mars.

The system uses a mobile robotic platform equipped with an extendable robotic arm and gripping mechanism. It approaches discarded equipment, securely collects selected objects and transfers them into an enclosed storage compartment. The recovered material can then be inspected, sorted, documented and assessed for potential reuse or safe storage.

The project's objective is to explore how robotic technology can support responsible management of abandoned space hardware, preserve valuable resources and reduce unnecessary accumulation of equipment on planetary surfaces.
details: COSCOM ROVER (Robotic Operations for Valuable Equipment Recovery) is a conceptual robotic system proposed for the responsible recovery and management of abandoned human-made equipment on the Moon and Mars. The system uses a mobile rover equipped with an extendable robotic arm and gripping mechanism to identify, retrieve and securely store selected abandoned objects. Recovered equipment can subsequently be inspected, documented and evaluated for potential reuse or safe storage. A Python-based 2D simulation demonstrates the proposed rover movement, robotic-arm operation, object retrieval and storage process. The project aims to explore how robotic technology can contribute to sustainable planetary exploration while protecting valuable scientific and historical equipment.
